title: INT 13h, the BIOS disk services
covers: INT 13h, the BIOS disk services: floppy and hard disk calls and the INT 13h extensions.

rows.text: INT 13h AH=00h resets the disk system.
DL is the drive number.
If bit 7 of DL is set, both hard disks and floppy disks are reset.
AH returns the status of the operation.
CF is clear if the call succeeded.
On success the returned AH is 00h.
CF is set on error.
The call forces the controller to recalibrate the drive heads (seek to track 0).
On PS/2 35SX, 35LS, 40SX and L40SX and many other systems, master and slave drive both respond to a Reset issued to either.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x0, with AH as the selector.
With DL 0x80 or above it calls the IDE reset for DL and recalibrates an IDE disk; only a DL below 0x80 calls the floppy reset.
The status of the call goes to last_status: NoError (0x00) on success and BadCommand (0x01) for a missing drive.
On success the case stores no reg_ah, so AH is whatever it held at the call.
With an image mounted, a missing drive sets CF and status 0x01, except on CGA, Amstrad, PCjr, Olivetti and 3270 PC machines with floppy 0 or 1 active: CF clear.
In that inactive-drive exception, a DL below 0x80 on a machine other than a PCjr also increments the guest's IP by one.
Unless the machine is a PCjr, a DL below 0x80 increments the guest's IP by one before the reset.
The handler sets the guest's interrupt flag before it dispatches on AH.
With the INT 13h extensions disabled, a call with AH from 0x40 to 0x48 returns AH 0xFF and CF set before any case.
INT 13h AH=01h gets the status of the last operation.
DL is the drive, with bit 7 set for a hard disk.
CF is clear if successful, when the returned status is 00h.
CF is set on error.
AH is the status of the previous operation.
Some BIOSes return the status in AL; the PS/2 Model 30/286 returns it in both AH and AL.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x1, with AH as the selector.
This case does not use DL: it returns the one last_status of the previous call, whatever drive that call named.
This case stores no reg_al: the status goes to AH only.
driveInactive stores BadCommand for a drive with no image, where the CHS read returns AH=0xff, so this case then returns BadCommand; reset and the three reads store NoError on success.
INT 13h AH=02h reads sectors into memory.
The call reads the requested sectors from the disk into memory.
AL is the number of sectors to read.
AL must be nonzero.
CH is the low eight bits of the cylinder; bits 6-7 of CL are its high two bits, hard disk only.
Bits 0-5 of CL are the sector number, 1 to 63.
DH is the head number.
DL is the drive number, with bit 7 set for a hard disk.
ES:BX points to the data buffer.
CF is set on error.
If AH is 11h (corrected ECC error), AL is the burst length.
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the status of the operation.
AL is the number of sectors transferred (only valid if CF set for some BIOSes).
Floppy errors may be due to a slow motor spin-up; retry at least three times, resetting the disk with AH=00h between attempts.
Most BIOSes support multitrack reads: an AL past the end of the track reads on from sector 1 of the next head in the same cylinder.
The CONFIG.SYS command MULTITRACK, or DEBLOCK= in Novell DOS, makes DOS split accesses that would wrap across a track.
The IBM AT BIOS and many other BIOSes use only the low four bits of DH, the head number.
AWARD AT BIOS and AMI 386sx BIOS handle more than 1024 cylinders by putting cylinder bits 10 and 11 into bits 6 and 7 of DH.
Under Windows95 a volume must be locked before direct accesses such as INT 13h reads and writes.
All versions of MS-DOS cannot boot from hard disks with 256 heads, so many BIOSes give at most 255 heads.
Some cache drivers flush their buffers when INT 13h is issued directly; a dummy read can force the flush.
Reading floppies, some AMI BIOSes (around 1990-1991) trash the byte after the buffer if it is not on an even boundary.
A workaround is to make the buffer word aligned, or to add a dummy byte after it.
MS-DOS may leave interrupts disabled on return from this function.
Apparently some BIOSes or intercepting software may destroy DX on return or not set the Carry flag properly.
At least some Microsoft software frames calls to this function with PUSH DX, STC, INT 13h, STI, POP DX.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x2, which returns INT13_ReadSectors.
AH is 0x00, 0x01, 0x06, 0x80 or the sector read's status.
The read-error exit stores AH and sets CF but stores no reg_al, so AL is not the sectors transferred.
The read-error path stores AH and sets CF at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:444-445, logging at 438; AL is not stored.
A hard disk takes bits 0-5 of CL as the first sector; a floppy takes all eight bits of CL.
DH goes whole, all eight bits, to the sector read as the head number; the cylinder comes from CH and CL only.
Cylinder bits 10 and 11 are not taken from DH: a hard disk's cylinder has ten bits, from CH and bits 6-7 of CL; a floppy's is CH alone.
The buffer copy writes transfer_size bytes with one real_writeb each; no byte after them is written there.
A drive with no image fails with status and AH 0x01 and CF set unless it is a mounted DOS drive that is not removable.
On a mounted fixed DOS drive with no image, DL bit 7, DH 0, sector 1 succeeds; with CH 0 it first writes 0x80 at ES:BX+0x1BE and 0x06 at ES:BX+0x1C2.
A drive whose sectors exceed 8192 bytes fails with status and AH 0x80 and CF set, and its disk-change flag is cleared.
On a floppy whose disk-change flag is set, the read fails once with status and AH 0x06 and CF set, and clears the flag.
A sector read with status 0x10, a data error, is still copied to ES:BX before the read fails.
While killRead is set, a read copies nothing and fails, with status 0x04 unless the sector read returned an error status, which is kept; the flag is then cleared.
A floppy transfers the bytes per sector of the INT 1Eh table, 512 if the vector is null or the size code above 6; a hard disk 512.
An inactive drive gives AH 0xFF while last_status holds 0x01.

The call writes the requested sectors from memory to the disk.
AL is the number of sectors to write.
AL must be nonzero.
CH is the low eight bits of the cylinder; bits 6-7 of CL are its high two bits, hard disk only.
Bits 0-5 of CL are the sector number, 1 to 63.
DH is the head number.
DL is the drive number, with bit 7 set for a hard disk.
ES:BX points to the data buffer.
CF is set on error.
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the status of the operation.
AL is the number of sectors transferred (only valid if CF set for some BIOSes).
Floppy errors may be due to a slow motor spin-up; retry at least three times, resetting the disk with AH=00h between attempts.
Most BIOSes support multitrack writes: an AL past the end of the track writes on from sector 1 of the next head in the same cylinder.
The CONFIG.SYS command MULTITRACK makes DOS split accesses that would wrap across a track boundary into two calls.
The IBM AT BIOS and many other BIOSes use only the low four bits of DH, the head number.
AWARD AT BIOS and AMI 386sx BIOS handle more than 1024 cylinders by putting cylinder bits 10 and 11 into bits 6 and 7 of DH.
Under Windows95 an application must issue a physical volume lock on the drive before it can write to the disk with this function.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x3, with AH as the selector.
AH is 0x00, 0x80 or the sector write's status; a missing or inactive drive gives 0xFF.
The write-error exit stores AH and sets CF but stores no reg_al, so AL is not the sectors transferred.
After the drive and sector-size checks, a zero AL is not refused: the sector loop runs no time and the call ends with AH 0x00 and CF clear.
A hard disk takes bits 0-5 of CL as the first sector; a floppy takes all eight bits of CL.
DH goes whole, all eight bits, to the sector write as the head number; the cylinder comes from CH and CL only.
Cylinder bits 10 and 11 are not taken from DH: a hard disk's cylinder has ten bits, from CH and bits 6-7 of CL; a floppy's is CH alone.
A drive whose sectors exceed 2048 bytes fails with AH 0x80 and CF set, and its disk-change flag is cleared.
A floppy writes the INT 1Eh table's bytes per sector (512 if the vector is null or the code above 6), a hard disk the image's, clamped to 2048.
INT 13h AH=04h verifies disk sectors.
AL is the number of sectors to verify.
AL must be nonzero.
CH is the low eight bits of the cylinder; bits 6-7 of CL are its high two bits, hard disk only.
Bits 0-5 of CL are the sector number, 1 to 63.
DH is the head number.
DL is the drive number, with bit 7 set for a hard disk.
ES:BX points to a data buffer, on the PC, XT and AT with a BIOS prior to 1985/11/15.
CF is set on error.
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the status of the operation.
AL is the number of sectors verified.
Floppy errors may be a slow motor spin-up (timeout 80h); retry at least three times, resetting the disk with AH=00h between attempts.
On floppies the operation should also be retried when media change (06h) is detected.
The function does not compare the disk with memory; it only checks whether the sector's stored CRC matches the data's actual CRC.
The IBM AT BIOS and many other BIOSes use only the low four bits of DH, the head number.
AWARD AT BIOS and AMI 386sx BIOS handle more than 1024 cylinders by putting cylinder bits 10 and 11 into bits 6 and 7 of DH.
The workaround for the problem is to reset the disk (INT 13h AH=00h) before the call.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x04, with AH as the selector.
With non-zero AL and an active drive it calls no sector read and compares no CRC: after the floppy or IDE access routine it returns AH 0x00 and CF clear.
AL goes as the sector count to the floppy or IDE access routine; this case calls no sector read.
Only a floppy and an IDE disk are passed a cylinder: a floppy CH whole, an IDE disk CH plus bits 6-7 of CL.
An IDE hard disk takes bits 0-5 of CL as the sector; a floppy passes all eight bits of CL.
DH is passed whole to the floppy and IDE access routines; the floppy routine's first statement is (void)head.
This case's own lines never read ES or BX.
This case's own lines store no reg_al, so AL keeps the value it had at the call.
DH goes whole, all eight bits, as the head argument to the floppy and IDE access routines; the IDE one computes its LBA from it.
Cylinder bits 10 and 11 are not taken from DH: an IDE disk's cylinder has ten bits, from CH and bits 6-7 of CL.
Only DL 0x00, 0x01 and 0x80 to 0x83 map to a drive; any other DL is not an active drive.
INT 13h AH=05h formats a floppy track.
The call formats a track of the floppy.
AL is the number of sectors to format.
CH is the track number.
DH is the head number.
DL is the drive number.
ES:BX points to the address field buffer (see #00235).
CF is set on error.
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the status of the operation.
On an AT or higher, call AH=17h first.
The number of sectors per track is read from the diskette parameter table pointed at by INT 1Eh.
A possible workaround for the problem is to call from real mode, through DPMI "Call Real Mode function with FAR return".
Each address field buffer entry is four bytes: track, head (0-based), sector number, sector size code (00h=128, 01h=256, 02h=512, 03h=1024).
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x05, with AH as the selector.
The case logs that format is ignored and, for a floppy, calls the floppy access routine with the Format op, sector 1 and count 0.
The case calls FLOPPY_INT13_Access and stores AH and CF at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:643-644, logging at 635; AL is not read.
Only a floppy drive is passed CH, as the cylinder argument of the floppy access routine.
A floppy drive's access routine is passed DH as the head, and its first statement is (void)head.
The case calls FLOPPY_INT13_Access and stores AH and CF at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:643-644, logging at 635; ES and BX are not read.
AH is 0x00 on success; an inactive drive gives 0xFF.
The case calls FLOPPY_INT13_Access and stores AH and CF at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:643-644, logging at 635; the INT 1Eh table is not read.
The case calls FLOPPY_INT13_Access and stores AH and CF at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:643-644, logging at 635; no address field buffer is read.

The call formats a track and sets bad sector flags.
AL is the interleave value.
CH is the cylinder number, with bits 8 and 9 in the high bits of CL.
CL is the sector number.
DH is the head.
DL is the drive.
AH is the status code (see #00234).
AWARD AT BIOS and AMI 386sx BIOS handle more than 1024 cylinders by putting cylinder bits 10 and 11 into bits 6 and 7 of DH.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x06, with AH as the selector.
Nothing is formatted and no flag is set: the case logs that the bad-sector flags are ignored and then returns.
AH is 0x00 on success; an inactive drive gives 0xFF.
CF is set only for an inactive drive and is clear otherwise.
The case stores AH and sets CF at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:654-655, logging at 648; AL is not read.

The call formats the drive starting at a given track.
AL is the interleave value (XT only).
ES:BX is a 512-byte format buffer (see AH=05h).
CH is the cylinder number, with bits 8 and 9 in the high bits of CL.
CL is the sector number.
DH is the head.
DL is the drive.
AH is the status code (see #00234).

The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x07, with AH as the selector.
Nothing is formatted and no flag is set: the case logs that the bad-sector flags are ignored and then returns.
AH is 0x00 on success; an inactive drive gives 0xFF.

The case stores AH and sets CF at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:665-666, logging at 659; AL is not read.

INT 13h AH=08h gets the drive parameters.
DL is the drive, with bit 7 set for a hard disk.
ES:DI should be 0000h:0000h before the call, to guard against BIOS bugs.
CF is set on error.
On error AH is the status, 07h (see #00234).
CF is clear if successful.
On success AH is 00h.
AL is 00h on at least some BIOSes.
BL is the drive type, for AT and PS/2 floppies only (see #00242).
CH is the low eight bits of the maximum cylinder number.
Bits 5-0 of CL are the maximum sector number.
Bits 7-6 of CL are the high two bits of the maximum cylinder number.
DH is the maximum head number.
DL is the number of drives.
ES:DI points to the drive parameter table, for floppies only.
It may return successful even though the drive is greater than the number of attached drives of that type.
Check DL to ensure the drive is valid.
The IBM ROM-BIOS returns the total number of hard disks attached, whether or not DL is 80h or more on entry.
The count in DL may indicate only two drives present even if more are attached.
To ensure a correct count, AH=15h can be used to scan through the possible drives.
The maximum cylinder in CX is usually two less than the cylinder count of the fixed disk parameter table; on some Zenith machines reportedly three less.
For BIOSes that reserve the last cylinder for testing, the cylinder count is automatically decremented.
The PC-Tools PCFORMAT program requires AL=00h before it proceeds with the formatting.
If this function fails, INT 11h gives another way to get the number of floppy drives installed.
MS-DOS IO.SYS tries this call for the floppy count when INT 11h shows none, and trusts it only if CL, preset to zero, returns non-zero.
As a workaround, scan the disk numbers, stopping when the valid drives found equal the value at 0040h:0075h.
AD-DOS may leave interrupts disabled on return from this function; some Microsoft software explicitly sets STI after return.
BL is 01h for a 360K, 02h for a 1.2M, 03h for a 720K and 04h for a 1.44M drive.
BL 05h is reportedly an obscure drive type shipped on some IBM machines; on some machines, at least with an AMI 486 BIOS, it is 2.88M.
BL 06h is a 2.88M drive and BL 10h an ATAPI Removable Media Device.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x08, with AH as the selector.
A missing drive 0 succeeds with fixed 1.44M values (BL 4, CH 79, CL 18, DH 1, DL 1) and ES:DI in the BIOS; another missing drive fails, AH 0x07.
BL comes from the image's BIOS type for every active drive, hard disks too.
A hard disk gets bits 5-0 of CL from the sector count; a floppy gets the sector count in all eight bits.
Only a hard disk gets the high two bits of the maximum cylinder in bits 7-6 of CL; a floppy has none.
DL below 0x80 returns the count of floppy images 0 and 1; DL of 0x80 or more returns the count of hard disk images.
The count in DL is not limited to two: a hard disk call counts every mounted image from index 2.
The maximum cylinder is the image's cylinder count less one and less its reserved-cylinder value.
A zero cylinder or head count is logged as an error and reported as 0.
Success stores 0x00 as the status that a later AH=0x01 returns.
Only DL 0x00, 0x01 and 0x80 to 0x83 map to a drive; any other DL is not an active drive.

rows.text: INT 13h AH=0Ch seeks a hard disk to a cylinder.
The call seeks the hard disk to the cylinder.
CH is the low eight bits of the cylinder number.
Bits 5-0 of CL are the sector number.
Bits 7-6 of CL are the high two bits of the cylinder number.
DH is the head number.
DL is the drive number, 80h for the first and 81h for the second hard disk.
CF is set on error.
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the status of the operation.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x0C, with AH as the selector.
The sector bits of CL are not read: the IDE seek call is passed sector 1.
AH is 0x01 for a DL below 0x80 and 0x00 on success; for an inactive hard disk this case stores no AH.
A DL below 0x80 fails with AH 0x01 and CF set.
DL 0x80 to 0x83 map to drives 2 to 5, so 0x82 and 0x83 are accepted too; any other DL is not an active drive.
An IDE hard disk is seeked through the IDE access call; any other active drive with DL 0x80 or above succeeds with AH 0x00 and CF clear, with no seek.
INT 13h AH=11h recalibrates a hard disk drive.
DL is the drive number, 80h for the first and 81h for the second hard disk.
CF is set on error.
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the status of the operation.
The call causes the hard disk controller to seek the drive to cylinder 0.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x11, with AH as the selector.
This case never sets CF: it ends with AH 0x00 and CF clear whatever the drive.
Only an IDE hard disk is recalibrated; any other DL, active or not, succeeds with AH 0x00 and CF clear.
DL 0x80 to 0x83 map to drives 2 to 5, so 0x82 and 0x83 are recalibrated too when IDE; another DL from 0x80 maps to drive 0x7f, past MAX_DISK_IMAGES.
INT 13h AH=15h gets the disk type.
DL is the drive number, with bit 7 set for a hard disk.
Call with AL=FFh and CX=FFFFh preset (see the Note).
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the type code.
AH 00h means no such drive.
AH 01h is a floppy without change-line support; 02h is a floppy, or other removable drive, with change-line support.
AH 03h is a hard disk, and CX:DX is its number of 512-byte sectors.
CF is set on error.
On error AH is the status (see #00234).
Some PC Tools REBUILD releases preset CX=FFFFh and trust the result only if CH is 2 or less on return.
As a workaround, scan the disk numbers, stopping when the valid drives found equal the value at 0040h:0075h.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x15, with AH as the selector.
A drive that does not exist fails with CF set: AH 0x07 when an image is mounted, 0xFF when none is.
With images mounted a hard disk's CX:DX is the image size in sectors and a floppy's are untouched; with none, a hard disk reports a fixed 0x0003:0x4800.
Only DL 0x00, 0x01 and 0x80 to 0x83 map to a drive; any other DL is not an active drive.
INT 13h AH=16h detects a floppy disk change.
DL is the drive number, 00h to 7Fh.
SI should be 0000h, to avoid a crash on the AT&T 6300.
If the change line is inactive, CF is clear and AH is 00h (disk not changed).
If the change line is active, CF is set and AH is the status.
AH 06h means the change line is active or not supported.
AH 80h means the drive is not ready or not present.
Call AH=15h first to find out whether the drive supports a change line.
The call also clears the media-change status, so a disk change is reported only once.
Some drives (or controllers???) forget the change line status if another drive is accessed; the DOS BIOS then reports "don't know" to the kernel.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x16, with AH as the selector.
Only DL 0x00 and 0x01 map to a floppy; a DL of 0x02 to 0x7F maps to no drive and fails with AH 0x80.
With change detection enabled and no change flagged, CF is clear and AH 0x00; with it disabled the call fails with AH 0xFF and CF set.
AH 0x06 with CF set when a floppy's change flag is set or for a hard disk; with detection disabled the call returns 0xFF instead.

AL is the format type.
AL 01h is a 320/360K disk in a 360K drive and 02h a 320/360K disk in a 1.2M drive.
AL 03h is a 1.2M disk in a 1.2M drive and 04h a 720K disk in a 720K or 1.44M drive.
DL is the drive number.
CF is set on error.
CF is clear if successful.
AH is the status of the operation.
This function does not handle 1.44M drives; use AH=18h instead.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x17, with AH as the selector.
The format type is ignored: the call sets killRead, which makes the next sector read fail, and succeeds.
This case's own lines never read reg_al, so 01h and 02h are not distinguished.
This case's own lines never read reg_al, so 03h and 04h are not distinguished.
This case's own lines never read reg_dl or the drive number.
This case never sets CF: it ends with AH 0x00 and CF clear.
INT 13h AH=41h checks whether the INT 13h extensions are installed.
BX is 55AAh.
DL is the drive, 80h to FFh.
CF is set on error, when the extensions are not supported.
On error AH is 01h (invalid function).
CF is clear if successful.
BX is AA55h if the extensions are installed.
AH is the major version of the extensions; 01h is 1.x.
AH 20h is 2.0 or EDD-1.0, 21h is 2.1 or EDD-1.1, and 30h is EDD-3.0.
AL is for internal use.
CX is the API subset support bitmap (see #00271).
DH is the extension version (v2.0+ ??? -- not present in 1.x).
Bit 0 of CX set means the extended disk access functions (AH=42h-44h, 47h, 48h) are supported.
Bit 1 of CX set means the removable drive controller functions (AH=45h, 46h, 48h, 49h, INT 15h AH=52h) are supported.
Bit 2 of CX set means the enhanced disk drive functions (AH=48h, 4Eh) are supported and the extended drive parameter table is valid.
Bits 3 to 15 of CX are reserved (0).
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x41, with AH as the selector.
Only DL 0x00, 0x01 and 0x80 to 0x83 map to a drive; the call needs an active image on it, and a floppy DL is accepted.
A refused call stores no AH, which stays 0x41; with the extensions disabled the handler returns AH 0xFF.
The success branch stores AH, BX and CX at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:858-860, logging at 857, with CX set to 0x0001 only.
The success branch stores AH, BX and CX at src/ints/bios_int13.cpp:858-860, logging at 857, with CX set to 0x0001 only.

INT 13h AH=42h reads sectors with the INT 13h extensions.
The call reads the blocks of the disk address packet into memory.
DL is the drive number.
DS:SI points to the disk address packet (see #00272).
CF is clear if successful.
On success AH is 00h.
CF is set on error.
On error AH is the error code (see #00234).
On error the packet's block count field is set to the number of blocks successfully transferred.
The packet starts with its size, 10h or 18h, and a reserved byte of 0.
At offset 02h is the number of blocks to transfer, at most 007Fh for the Phoenix EDD.
At offset 04h is a DWORD pointing to the transfer buffer.
At offset 08h is the starting absolute block number, a QWORD.
For non-LBA devices compute the block as (Cylinder*NumHeads + SelectedHead) * SectorPerTrack + SelectedSector - 1.
At offset 10h is an optional EDD-3.0 QWORD flat address of the transfer buffer, used if the DWORD at 04h is FFFFh:FFFFh.
The INT 13h handler reaches it by its case 0x42, which returns INT13_ExtendedReadSectors.
AH is 0x01 for a refused packet, 0x80 for oversize sectors, 0xFF for an inactive drive, else the status of the sector read.
On error the count is the failing sector's index, plus one when its data was copied despite a data error.
Only a packet of size 0x10 with a reserved byte of 0 is accepted; others log a warning and fail with AH 0x01.
A count of zero fails with AH 0x01; otherwise the loop transfers one block per unit of sector_count, a 16-bit word read from the packet.
Only the low dword of the block number is used; a nonzero high dword logs a warning and fails with AH 0x01.
The flat buffer form is not supported: a packet of size 0x18 is refused with AH 0x01.
A DL equal to the El Torito no-emulation drive number is read through INT13_ReadElToritoSectors, which is not followed here.
With a valid packet and no image mounted, DL bit 7, DH 0 and sector 1 in CL succeed with AH 0x00 and CF clear, without a transfer.
A drive whose sectors exceed 8192 bytes fails with status and AH 0x80 and CF set.
While killRead is set, a read copies nothing and fails, with status 0x04 unless the sector read returned an error status, which is kept; the flag is then cleared.
A sector read with status 0x10, a data error, is still copied to the buffer before the read fails.
INT 13h AH=43h writes sectors with the INT 13h extensions.
The call writes the blocks of the disk address packet from memory to the disk.
AL is the write flags.
In versions 1.0 and 2.0, bit 0 of AL requests a verified write.
In versions 1.0 and 2.0, bits 7 to 1 of AL are reserved (0).
In versions 2.1 and later, AL 00h or 01h writes without verify and 02h writes with verify.
DL is the drive number.
DS:SI points to the disk address packet (see #00272).
CF is clear if successful.
On success AH is 00h.
